# `md/no-duplicate-heading`

**No two sibling headings with the same text**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-data` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-data` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | Markdown |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:md/recommended` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `siblings_only` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (which heading to rename, and to what, needs the author) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.1.0 |
| **Ported from** | `markdownlint/MD024` |

## What it checks

Headings under the same parent heading have different text.

**Why:** Readers and tables of contents tell sections apart by their headings, and repeated headings get anchors (`#setup`, `#setup-1`) that are easy to link to the wrong one.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-data
pip install codelaw-rules-data
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:md/recommended` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:md/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"md/no-duplicate-heading" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `siblings_only` | `boolean` | `true` | only compare headings under the same parent; `false` compares every heading in the document |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."md/no-duplicate-heading"]
severity = "error"

[rules."md/no-duplicate-heading".options]
siblings_only = true
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"md/no-duplicate-heading" = { severity = "error", options = { siblings_only = false } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `siblings_only`

*boolean* · default `true`

only compare headings under the same parent; `false` compares every heading in the document

```toml
[rules."md/no-duplicate-heading".options]
siblings_only = false
```

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.md"]
rules = { "md/no-duplicate-heading" = { options = { siblings_only = false } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.md"]
rules = { "md/no-duplicate-heading" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"md/no-duplicate-heading" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"md/no-duplicate-heading" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"md/no-duplicate-heading" = { severity = "warn", options = { siblings_only = false } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "md/no-duplicate-heading": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"siblings_only": false}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **Markdown:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore md/no-duplicate-heading: <reason> -->`
- **Dated:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore md/no-duplicate-heading expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> -->`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule md/no-duplicate-heading --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain md/no-duplicate-heading       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule md/no-duplicate-heading  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>           # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Decide whether the two sections are one topic; if so, merge them.
2. Otherwise rename one heading to say how it differs.

## Examples

### Markdown

#### Don't

````md
# Tools

## Setup

Install the CLI.

## Setup

Configure it.
````

#### Do

````md
# Tools

## Setup

Install the CLI.

## Configuration

Configure it.
````

## Differences from the source

`siblings_only` defaults to `true` here (markdownlint defaults it to `false`), so a changelog's repeated `### Fixed` under each version is not reported.
